name: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
alternateNames: Dormition of the Mother of God
ecclesialTitle: Solemnity of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
briefBio: The Assumption celebrates the Church's confession that Mary, having completed her earthly life, was taken body and soul into heavenly glory. It is not a report of her final address, medical condition, place of death, or the mechanics of the event. Eastern Dormition and Western Assumption traditions developed through diverse liturgical and narrative witnesses. The solemnity points to Christ's resurrection and the promised renewal of the whole human person. Mary's glory is received from God and anticipates the hope offered to Christ's people.

editorial.reviewer: Catholic Daily factual and theological review

whyItMatters: The Assumption turns Christian hope toward the resurrection of the whole person. Mary's glory is God's gift in Christ, not escape from embodied life; it strengthens care for bodies, creation, grief, and faithful work while believers await renewal.
oneMinuteSummary: On August 15 the Church celebrates that Mary, after completing her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory. The 1950 definition deliberately does not settle whether she died or describe a place, witnesses, medical condition, or physical mechanism. Ancient Dormition and Assumption traditions are diverse and become clearly visible in fifth- and sixth-century sources; they should not be compressed into one eyewitness biography. The solemnity is centered on Christ: Mary's glorification depends entirely on his death and resurrection and anticipates the bodily future promised to his people. It therefore honors the body without denying grief, illness, disability, aging, or death. Hope in resurrection supports present responsibility rather than escape. Believers can celebrate through Eucharistic worship, prayer, care for vulnerable bodies, and patient work for a world in which human dignity is protected while creation awaits renewal.

sections.heading: What the Church celebrates
sections.body: The solemnity confesses Mary's bodily glorification by God after the completion of her earthly life. It celebrates a mystery of grace, not an independently witnessed modern-style chronology.

sections.heading: Tradition and historical limits
sections.body: Dormition and Assumption accounts emerged in varied languages and forms. Their diversity witnesses developing reception but does not establish one detailed account of Mary's last days, death, tomb, or transfer.

sections.heading: A sign of resurrection hope
sections.body: Mary's glory is wholly dependent on Christ and anticipates the Church's promised fulfillment. Bodily hope must deepen respect for embodied people now, never dismiss pain or replace medical care.

life.gospelTheme: The risen Christ will transform his people; Mary's Assumption is received as a sign of that promised bodily future.
life.struggle: Devotion can turn the mystery into invented biography, speculation about death, or an escape from bodily suffering and present duties.
life.response: The Church keeps the definition precise, receives historical traditions in their proper genre, and lives resurrection hope through worship and care for embodied neighbors.

virtues.name: Embodied hope
virtues.evidence: The definition includes Mary's body and directs attention to Christ's victory over death.
virtues.imitation: Treat one vulnerable person's bodily needs with patience and practical dignity rather than offering only spiritual words.

virtues.name: Humble discernment
virtues.evidence: The dogmatic formula does not decide details that diverse later narratives supply.
virtues.imitation: Name what faith teaches and what history cannot establish instead of making certainty more dramatic than the evidence.

practice.spiritual: Pray 1 Corinthians 15:42–44 slowly and entrust your whole embodied life to the risen Christ.
practice.action: Offer ten practical minutes to protect bodily dignity: prepare food, check accessibility, accompany someone safely, or support needed rest and care.

reflectionQuestions: Does my resurrection hope make me more attentive to bodies and suffering now?
Can I cherish sacred tradition without inventing certainty about Mary's final days?

scripture.connection: Paul's proclamation of bodily resurrection supplies the Christian horizon in which Mary's Assumption is celebrated as a sign of hope in Christ.

prayer: Risen Lord Jesus, you have conquered death and promise renewal to your people. As we celebrate Mary's Assumption, strengthen our hope, teach us to honor every body, and keep us faithful in present duties while we await your kingdom. Amen.
